description:
The Collaborative Research Scheme (CRS) is an initiative launched by the Government of India in 2016. 

The scheme aims to promote collaborative research between Indian researchers and international scientists. 

It focuses on enhancing the quality of research output in various scientific domains. 

The CRS is administered by the Department of Science and Technology (DST) under the Ministry of Science and Technology. 

The primary objective of the CRS is to foster international collaboration in research. 

It seeks to create a platform for Indian researchers to work alongside global experts. 

The scheme aims to enhance the visibility of Indian research on the global stage. 

It also aims to facilitate the exchange of knowledge and technology between India and other countries. 

The CRS targets specific areas of research that are of national importance. 

These areas include health, agriculture, energy, and environmental science. 

The scheme has set measurable targets for the number of collaborative projects funded annually. 

In the initial phase, the CRS aimed to support at least 50 collaborative projects each year. 

The funding provided under the CRS can go up to INR 50 lakhs per project. 

This funding is intended to cover various research expenses including equipment, materials, and travel. 

The duration of each project funded under the CRS can be up to three years. 

Eligible applicants for the CRS must be Indian researchers affiliated with recognized institutions. 

These institutions include universities, research organizations, and public sector undertakings. 

The researchers must have a proven track record in their respective fields. 

There are no specific age limits for applicants under the CRS. 

However, researchers must demonstrate their capability to lead collaborative projects. 

The CRS encourages proposals that include participation from at least one international partner. 

This international partner must be a recognized research institution or university. 

The application process for the CRS involves several steps. 

First, researchers must prepare a detailed project proposal. 

This proposal should outline the research objectives, methodology, and expected outcomes. 

Researchers must also include a budget breakdown detailing how the funds will be utilized. 

The proposal must be submitted online through the DST's official portal. 

Along with the proposal, applicants must submit their curriculum vitae. 

They must also provide letters of support from the international partner institution. 

Once submitted, the proposals undergo a rigorous evaluation process. 

This evaluation is conducted by a panel of experts in the relevant field. 

The panel assesses the scientific merit and feasibility of the proposed research. 

Successful applicants are notified within three months of submission. 

Funding is disbursed in installments based on project milestones. 

The first installment is released upon project approval. 

Subsequent installments are released upon the submission of progress reports. 

These reports must detail the research activities undertaken and expenditures incurred. 

The CRS also emphasizes the importance of disseminating research findings. 

Researchers are encouraged to publish their results in peer-reviewed journals. 

They must also present their findings at national and international conferences. 

The scheme has seen a steady increase in participation since its inception. 

In 2021, the CRS funded a total of 75 collaborative projects. 

This represented a 50 percent increase in the number of projects funded compared to 2020. 

The total funding allocated for the CRS in the financial year 2021-2022 was INR 30 crores. 

This funding was aimed at supporting innovative research that addresses societal challenges. 

The CRS has also established partnerships with various international funding agencies. 

These partnerships aim to leverage additional resources for collaborative research. 

The scheme aligns with the Government of India's vision of "Atmanirbhar Bharat." 

This vision emphasizes self-reliance and innovation in research and development. 

The CRS also contributes to the global scientific community by fostering international cooperation. 

It encourages researchers to explore new frontiers in science and technology. 

The scheme has been instrumental in enhancing India's research capabilities. 

It has also helped in building long-term relationships between Indian and international researchers. 

The CRS is part of a broader strategy to enhance India's position in global research rankings. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from the research community. 

Researchers have reported increased opportunities for collaboration and funding. 

The CRS has also been recognized for its role in promoting interdisciplinary research. 

It encourages projects that combine expertise from different scientific fields. 

The scheme has a dedicated website that provides detailed information and updates. 

Researchers can access guidelines, application forms, and contact information on this site. 

The CRS is continuously evolving to meet the changing needs of the research landscape. 

It aims to adapt to emerging scientific challenges and opportunities. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of research ethics and integrity. 

Researchers are required to adhere to ethical standards in their work. 

The CRS has contributed significantly to India's scientific advancements. 

It has played a crucial role in addressing pressing national and global issues. 

The scheme is expected to continue growing in scope and impact in the coming years. 

Overall, the Collaborative Research Scheme represents a significant investment in India's scientific future. 

It embodies the government's commitment to fostering innovation and collaboration in research. 

The CRS is a vital tool for enhancing India's research capabilities on a global scale. 

It serves as a bridge between Indian researchers and the international scientific community. 

Through this scheme, the government aims to create a vibrant research ecosystem in India. 

The CRS is a testament to the importance of collaboration in advancing scientific knowledge. 

It highlights the potential of joint research efforts to drive innovation and development. 

The scheme is poised to make a lasting impact on India's research landscape. 

It is a crucial step towards achieving excellence in science and technology.
